goal: A static Rust binary that reads what an agent produced and refuses the growth that should not be there, deleted or weakened tests, skips, stubs, swallowed errors, secrets, guardrail edits, dependency-direction violations, in milliseconds, with zero tokens, every finding as SARIF 2.1.0. `weeder check` judges a diff and may block; `weeder scan` judges the tree and never blocks; `weeder guard` is the law in git through hooks; `weeder bite` proves a test fails without its change. For maintainers drowning in agent-authored pull requests who need a deterministic gate before they read, for teams running agents on several harnesses who want one law, and for the garden's own fleets through pleach.

work.prompt:
You are a worker in a build loop. Make the checks below pass, honestly.
Nobody reviews your prose — only the verifier's verdict counts, so put all effort into the work itself.

## The goal
`weeder scan` reads the repository as it is, not a diff, and names repo-state hygiene: a path, command, flag or symbol cited in the docs that no longer exists; a public symbol nothing references; a TODO older than the configured age; a dependency pin far behind the registry. It never blocks: exit 0 or 3 only, findings at warning level. tend2's hygiene loop is its first consumer, citing `weeder scan --format sarif` as evidence; `docs/tend2-seam.md` is the proposal for that seam.

## Your environment
- You are at the repository root of an isolated git worktree. Work here directly.
- Leave your changes in the working tree; do not create branches, commit, or push.
- The loop file (docs/tend2/scan.tend2.html) is your full context — read it, including its narrative. It is READ-ONLY for you.

## Checks to close
- (code) R1 keeps the `:line` or `:start-end` a citation carries and, when the path resolves, reports a line past the end of the file under the same rule id with its own sentence naming the file's line count; a bare name in a code span resolves as a symbol at warn only where a path citation on the same line, or the nearest preceding one in the same section that resolves, anchors it, against that file's outline first and the whole tree second, with the message naming the file; an unanchored name resolves against the whole tree and is reported at note; a citation resolving to a directory anchors the names after it to everything under it and the message names the directory · evidence expected at: tests/rule_r1.rs

## Definition of done — verify yourself before finishing
You are done when this exact command exits 0 (it is the gate the conductor will run):

    tend2 verify docs/tend2/scan.tend2.html --repo-root . --force --expect-payload d339500818c5 --runner 'bash scripts/check/run.sh {evidence}'

Run it yourself. If it does not exit 0, you are not done. Do not declare success in prose that a command disagrees with.

## Already tried (do not repeat)
- 2026-09-05 settled with tend2 on the channel (umbrella loop, 2026-09-05): `scan` owns repo-state hygiene and never blocks; tend2 keeps doc-evidence staleness and its hygiene loop pattern; `tend2 gate` and `weeder check` are different questions and both emit SARIF
- 2026-09-05 R4 never reaches the network during `scan`; the snapshot is a committed file so the rule is reproducible in CI
- 2026-09-05 cape-town: tend2 is scan's first consumer and is on pollen; before R1 to R4 are finalised, ask tend2 which SARIF fields its hygiene loop reads (asked the same day; the answer goes here, and this loop is not dispatched until it lands or tend2 says it has no preference)
- 2026-09-05 `garden.json` lists the faces the binary answers and `tests/garden_manifest.rs` holds it equal to `weeder --help`; this loop adds `scan` to the manifest's `faces` and to `SKILL.md`, or that test fails at its own gate
- 2026-09-05 cape-town: do not wait on tend2. Emit the minimal SARIF every consumer reads (ruleId, level, message.text, locations[0].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri, region.startLine) plus `properties.path` on each result for per-path aggregation; tend2's eventual answer is additive fields, never a change to those. Dispatched on that
- 2026-09-05 built by pleach node `scan` (claude/opus, codex audit) in one attempt, 45 minutes, landed by hand after `pleach land` met the rules-tests landing in `src/core/syntax.rs` and the fixtures README. The face reads the tree as it sits and leaves with 0 or 3; R1 resolves paths against the tree and commands against their own help through a new exec seam with a five-second deadline (`[docs] commands` names which); R2 exempts entry files, `main`, dunder names and runner prefixes; R3 asks git to blame only the files that carry a marker; R4 measures against `.weeder/registry-snapshot.json` and `--refresh-snapshot` fetches through curl so the binary stays a judge. Every result carries `properties.path`. Conductor review found nothing to fix
- 2026-09-05 `garden.json` and `SKILL.md` now name `scan`; `docs/tend2-seam.md` shows tend2's hygiene loop citing `weeder scan --format sarif` and proposes `weeder check` in place of its `mock.ts`, with `scripts/check/docs-tend2-seam.sh` running the commands it shows
- 2026-09-06 cape-town, after milestone 5: two binding checks before calibration dispatches. R1 executes nothing outside `[docs] commands`, only with `--help`, never through a shell, never with an argument from the document, proven on a fixture with a test-owned PATH; and a plain `weeder scan` is offline, proven under a denied network, with `weeder rules` naming which rules may reach the network and how. Shaped as the two checks above
- 2026-09-06 the two execution-bound checks landed by pleach node `scan` (claude/opus, codex audit) in one attempt, 28 minutes, through `pleach land`. The exec bound was already true and is now recorded by the commands themselves: a test-owned PATH whose programs write their own argv, two lines in the log (`listed-tool --help`, `listed-tool build --help`), the unlisted tool never called, no shell reached. The offline proof found a real defect: curl failing to resolve a host read as a registry with no latest release, so a refresh with no network wrote an empty snapshot and every pin would have read as current; a refresh now tells unreachable from unreadable, carries the committed value over for a package it could not ask about, and exits 3 leaving the snapshot untouched when it reached nothing. `weeder rules` carries a network column: `none` on every rule but R4, which says `registries under --refresh-snapshot`
- 2026-09-06 the offline proof failed on every CI run since it landed: GitHub's Ubuntu 24.04 runners restrict unprivileged user namespaces, so `unshare --user --net` could not start and the test refused, as designed, rather than pass on nothing. CI now lifts `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` before the suite, so the proof runs there for real. The conductor had reported CI green on the strength of an older run; watching the run is part of a push
- 2026-09-08 owner's issue 15: on an audited tree R1 produced 260 warnings, among them harness command names read as symbols, and the fifteen findings on the one document that mattered sat under 245 others; a cited `:479` in a 163-line file passed because `normalize()` cut the line before resolving. Shaped above as anchoring with a level split, which keeps every finding and changes only how loud it is; a `[docs] vocabulary` allowance list was rejected because it teaches a repository to write allowances for prose

## Rules
- Write the failing test first where it does not exist; then make it pass.
- You must not edit the loop file — check states belong to the verifier.
- You must not weaken, skip, or mock the unit under test to force a green; mocked-unit evidence is detected and refused.
- Solve the CLASS of problem the claim names, not the test's example inputs. Hardcoding fixture strings, phrases, or patterns from the check or its tests into source (lookup tables, regex lists, phrase maps) is refused work even when the test goes green — it is an answer key, not a product.
- If the claim cannot be met generically with what you have, that is a real finding: write BLOCKED.md naming the missing capability (a model, a library, a redesign, a split of the check into honest tiers) instead of faking generality.
- Production quality only: no stubs, no TODOs, no placeholder implementations; match the style of the surrounding code.
- Scratch (probes, experiments, packets, session logs) goes under `$TMPDIR`, written through the shell only, never with the Write or Edit tool, and never under `.loop-scratch/` or anywhere in this worktree: the collector stages every path the editor touched, a path outside the worktree kills the delivery, and the hygiene gate judges whatever is left in the tree, including its secret scan.
- If you are genuinely blocked, write BLOCKED.md at the repo root — what you tried, what stopped you, what a fix needs. An honest BLOCKED.md is a good outcome; a faked green is the worst possible one.
